meta.resume_protocol: Reply with 'Resume' plus a video link/file or picture batch to append to this master list.

how_agents_use_this: Quality bar, not a backlog. Apply the item that fits the current task.
CLAUDE.md wins on secrets, a11y, budget zero, and never starting an APK unless the user names the build.
Skip stack_exclusions unless the user asks.
When shipping UI, check ui_ux_and_branding + accessibility_and_semantics + DESIGN.md.
When shipping API, check security_and_trust. Trim payloads. No secrets in logs or responses.

security_and_trust: Hide source maps in production: Never ship .map files publicly; they expose full source code and internal logic.
Clean production console: No uncaught errors or stack traces visible to users.
Explicit payment confirmation: Show charged amount, masked card details, and receipt options after transactions.
Prevent double-submissions: Morph buttons into a disabled Processing spinner during async operations.
Document security decisions: Record auth and protection choices (JWT, rate limiting) in your tech doc.

Enforce server-side authorization (IDOR prevention): Authentication (who are you) is not authorization (what may you do); the server must pass every policy rule and deny by default on every request (OWASP Broken Access Control / CWE-639).
Complete logout checklist: Clear session token, cookies, localStorage, sessionStorage AND invalidate the token server-side.
Adversarial smoke tests: Paste a user URL into another browser; replay the URL after logout; confirm no data leaks.
AI-assisted security review pre-ship: Run /security-review (or equivalent) before deploying; it flags vulns with severity and exact fixes.
Never hardcode secrets client-side: API keys live server-side (environment variables), are rotated, and short-lived; frontend calls your own endpoint.
Frontend gets public limited keys only: Admin/full-access keys and admin consoles stay server-side/behind auth.
Sanitize untrusted input (XSS prevention): Output-escaping in all templates; textContent/DOMPurify over innerHTML; never store raw user input for later rendering.
Rate limit all public endpoints: Sliding-window request budgets per user + per app (e.g., 100 req/min), sensible defaults, graceful 429 retry-later responses.
Strict server-side input validation: Schema-based validation, type checks, length limits, reject unexpected fields.
Parameterize every database query: Prepared statements so form input is treated as data, not code (SQLi prevention).
Validate uploads + store outside web root: Check file type/size on every upload; store where files can never execute.
Verify webhook signatures: Reject unsigned/unverified payment events.
Give AI agents standing security rules: Persist security requirements in project-level rule files (e.g., CLAUDE.md).
Define an access control matrix: Document role x resource permissions explicitly.
Enforce HTTPS everywhere: Redirect HTTP to HTTPS at the proxy; no plaintext traffic.
Hash passwords properly: Salted, memory-hard KDF (scrypt/bcrypt/argon2); never store plaintext.
Bot protection on public forms: CAPTCHA (or equivalent) on signups and anonymous submission forms.
Enforce expiry: Session tokens expire server-side; password reset links are short-lived and single-use.
CSRF protection: Anti-CSRF tokens/defenses on all state-changing requests.
Least-privilege DB credentials: The app connects with a limited database user, never the master key.
No secrets in logs: Scrub passwords, card numbers, and tokens from application logs.
Billing/usage alerts: Alert on anomalous usage/cost so attacks are noticed immediately.
Automated backups: Scheduled, verified, restorable backups committed to up front.
Publish privacy policy & T&Cs: Missing legal pages are an instant trust/compliance red flag.
No fabricated social proof: Display real customer reviews; fake reviews/counters/metrics destroy credibility.
Checkout trust microcopy: Secure checkout / Encrypted reassurance beneath the pay button.
Treat deceptive UX as compliance risk: FTC Click-to-Cancel + California AB 2863; Amazon paid $2.5B over Prime tricks.
Entropy-based password strength policy: Score by entropy bits/crack-time, not character-class rules; length beats symbols; encourage passphrases.
Allow paste + reveal in password fields: Never block paste; provide show/hide toggle; password managers paste stronger unique passwords.
Offer suggested/generated passwords at signup: Use the OS/browser suggested-password pattern (generated, unique, saved to keychain); zero typing, weak choices, or reuse.

No backend details in user-facing errors: Friendly message client-side; full details (stack traces, connection strings, internal hosts) logged server-side only; exposure is a UX fail and a security vulnerability.
Purge secrets from Git history: Remove committed secrets from history (not just the working tree) and rotate them; .env + gitignore going forward.
Enable row-level security: DB-level RLS policies as defense-in-depth so a compromised app layer can't read every row.
Encrypt sensitive data at rest: Encrypt PII/payment/sensitive fields at rest; keys managed outside the database.
Secure session cookies: HttpOnly + Secure + SameSite flags on session cookies.
Trim API responses: Return only the fields the UI needs (least-privilege payloads); no accidental data leakage.
Add security headers: CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy on every response.
Scan dependencies: Automated dependency scanning (Dependabot/npm audit or equivalent) for known-vulnerable packages pre-launch and in CI.
technical_seo_and_metadata: Custom page titles: Unique, descriptive titles per route; no default framework titles.
Meta descriptions: Custom snippets so search engines don't auto-generate poor ones.
Social previews: og:image tags for proper link previews.
Structured data: JSON-LD schema for rich results, including LocalBusiness schema for local SEO.
Canonical tags: rel=canonical to prevent duplicate content.
Sitemaps: Generate an XML sitemap and submit it in Google Search Console (Indexing > Sitemaps) so Google grabs every page at once.
Multi-page information architecture: Avoid single-page sites for substantive products.
Indexing spot-check: Query site:yourdomain.com; zero results means you are invisible in search.
Register with Google Search Console: Add the property (free) and monitor the Pages report (indexed vs not-indexed).
Internal linking: Contextual internal links between related pages for navigation + SEO.
Breadcrumbs: Navigational breadcrumbs on nested pages for orientation + crawlability.
FAQ section (~5 questions): Answer the most common objections/questions on-page.
Maps + directions (local): Embed map/directions on local-business sites for trust + local SEO.
accessibility_and_semantics: Single H1 rule: Exactly one h1 per page.
Language attribute: Always set html lang.
Image alt text: Descriptive alt text on all images.
Full keyboard support for menus/dropdowns: Arrows navigate, Enter selects, Esc closes, every user, every time.
Full keyboard support for tabs: Arrows navigate, Home/End jump first/last, Tab exits the tablist; focus ring never looks the same as active state.
Accessible switches: Space toggles, visible focus ring, aria-checked state announced to screen readers.
Treat accessibility as a compliance requirement: Non-compliance is a legal liability; AI tools don't ship accessible output by default, so explicitly prompt for accessibility standards.
performance_and_build: Avoid empty source shells: Use SSR/SSG so the server builds the page, not the browser; complete HTML paints fast (~0.3s vs ~3.4s CSR), works on slow connections, and crawlers/social previews read real markup.
Optimize bundle size: Code-splitting and tree-shaking.
Document performance decisions: Record architecture choices (SSR, serverless, caching) in your tech doc.
Cache expensive results: Cache-first, database-second via Redis hot data (~1ms hit vs ~40ms DB); the hard part is freshness, so invalidate stale entries on write.

Async job queues for heavy tasks: Enqueue (email, invoice, inventory, warehouse) instead of making users wait on the sync path; independent workers (Kafka/RabbitMQ/SQS/Azure Service Bus) process jobs.
Index the database: Indexes turn million-row scans into ~20 comparisons; trade-off is write cost (+~35%) and storage for key copies, so index targeted queries.
Load test before launch: Stress-test with k6 (or equivalent) before real users arrive.
Horizontal scaling: Multiple stateless backend instances (session state in a shared store) behind a load balancer with health checks that route around failed instances (AWS ECS / Kubernetes).
Choose rendering strategy by content type: SSR for content-heavy public sites (blogs, news, storefronts, docs); CSR acceptable for highly interactive apps; trade-off is server load per request.
REST semantics: HTTP methods describe the action (GET retrieve, POST create, PUT replace, PATCH update-part, DELETE remove); status codes tell the result (200/400/401/403/500).
Atomic transactions: Multi-step writes commit all-or-nothing; any failure reverses the whole transaction; never leave partial state.
Serialize critical decisions (race conditions): Locks + unique constraints + atomic transactions yield one winner; no double-sold inventory.
Idempotency keys for safe retries: Same key returns the stored original response instead of re-executing; a retry must not charge twice.
Instrument analytics pre-launch: GA4 (or equivalent) installed before launch so behavior is measurable from day one.
ui_ux_and_branding: Custom domains: Own domain instead of default hosting subdomains.
Custom 404 pages: Branded, helpful error pages.
Favicons: Custom favicon for tab/bookmark recognition.
Mandatory action feedback: Every interaction gets immediate visual feedback; the silent failure (submit clicked, nothing changes) is the worst error state; explicitly instruct AI tools to prevent it.
Micro-interactions: Subtle animations for small actions (heart fill + count tick).
No silent high-stakes buttons: Confirm/Pay always need loading/success states.
Reserved celebrations: Confetti/full-page animations only for milestones.
Intuitive status indicators: Strikethroughs on done tasks, double-checks on read messages.
State-as-confirmation: Let the UI change itself replace toast pop-ups.
Map app flows pre-build: Diagram onboarding, journeys, button actions, success/error paths.
Write a design brief (DESIGN.md): Lock palette, typography, components, screen styles; save as a reusable skill/file your agent loads.
Avoid AI-default purple gradients: Applies to backgrounds and gradient hero headline text.
Replace AI-slop imagery: Use authentic photography, including a real team photo, instead of generic AI-generated visuals.
QA all CTAs: No broken or dead buttons at ship time.
Purposeful motion only: Skip gratuitous scroll-triggered animations on every section.
Real logo mark: Pair the wordmark with an icon; text-only logos read as unfinished.
SVG icon sets, not emoji: Emoji as feature icons is an instant tell.
Concrete hero value prop: State what the product does; avoid vague buzzword heroes.
Scrub AI tics pre-ship: Remove builder badges, cursive accent fonts, and em-dash-heavy copy.
Follow Jakob's Law (predictability over novelty): Keep standard components in conventional positions.
Avoid dark patterns (Roach Motel): Cancellation as easy as sign-up; no obstacle courses or guilt-trip copy.
Design all four screen states: Loading, success, error, and empty states on every screen.
Skeleton screens for content loads: Grey placeholder outlines pre-render layout before data arrives.
Match loader type to context: Skeletons / spinners / progress bars are not interchangeable.
Two-threshold swipe gestures: Reveal = menu; commit = decision.
Rubber-band resistance + haptic tick: Resistance is feedback; dies at commit with a haptic tick.
Consistent swipe direction semantics: Right = safe; Left = destructive. Never swap.
Teach gestures once: First-launch peek hint only.
Undo instead of confirm dialogs: Act immediately + timed Undo toast for destructive swipes.
Optimistic UI for reversible actions: Like/Follow/Save update instantly; under ~400ms reads as instant, waiting on the server reads as broken.
Rollback + error toast on optimistic failure: If the background sync fails, revert the state and explain; for async toggles, flip first with a spinner in the knob, then roll back on failure.
Show truth for irreversible actions: Pay/Transfer/Delete never render optimistically; display the real processing state.
Dropdown clickability: 48px+ touch target, visible-contrast border, clear caret icon, hover-state feedback.
Dropdown edge-flip: Detect viewport/container edges and flip the menu up instead of clipping it.
Comboboxes allow typing AND scrolling: 10+ options get a live filter input; filter beats scroll, but both paths stay available.
~150ms dropdown animation: Fast to feel instant, smooth to feel real.
Graceful degradation (per-section fault isolation): Each section owns its own fetch/loading/error+retry; one failure never crashes the page.
Validation timing (blur-first, then live): Validate on blur, dump remaining errors on submit, go live after the first error.
Confirm valid inputs: Show positive success affordances on valid fields; confirm right, not only wrong.
Star-rating hover preview: Hover previews the tentative rating; on mouse-leave, snap back to the committed value.
Honest aggregate ratings: Stop rounding up; render partial-star fill and summarize with a score ring + histogram.
Staggered star-fill animation: ~30ms left-to-right stagger; all-at-once reads flat.
Drag-and-drop feedback: Dropzone answers back on drag-over (border + glow + copy swap).
Honest upload progress: Show %, bar, time-left, and speed instead of an indeterminate spinner.
Resumable uploads with inline retry: On failure keep the file loaded; one-tap Retry resumes from the failed %.
Upload preview cards: Thumbnail, type, size, dimensions, uploaded-just-now proof, Replace/Remove actions.
Independent per-file upload queue: One lane per file; one failure never blocks the others.
Hold-to-confirm destructive actions: ~300ms progress ring replaces the Are-you-sure dialog; release early, nothing fires.
Verb-specific danger labels: Delete project / Keep project instead of Yes/No; the verb is the warning.
Keep destructive actions off the happy path: Never place destructive buttons in the primary click spot.
Red is a budget: Spend red on destruction/warnings only, and destructive CTAs (Delete account, etc.) must wear red per color psychology, never the brand primary.
Danger zone at the bottom: Group destructive settings in a bordered, labeled section last on the page.
Cooldown for irreversible actions: Schedule deletions with a grace period (e.g., 14 days) + Cancel escape hatch.
Sliding tab indicator: Underline slides (~280ms spring, ease-out) with ~180ms content fade; never a 0ms hard cut.
Tab overflow without wrapping: Never wrap to two lines; horizontal scroll + edge fades + chevrons on desktop.
Mobile tab strategy: <5 tabs segmented control; >5 tabs bottom-sheet section list; never shrink desktop tab bars; touch targets 44px+, thumb-zone first.
Tab content transitions: Fade-out 80ms, 80ms pause, fade-in 80ms; interpolate container height to avoid layout shift.
Toggle anatomy + morph transition: Rail width = 2x knob, padding = knob radius; morph rail color, knob slide, knob shadow, and OFF-to-ON label at ~250ms ease-out; never snap.
Live password-requirements checklist: Show rules before submit; chips turn green as satisfied while typing; never reveal red rules only after submit.
Strength meter coaches while typing: Segmented growing bar (Weak/Fair/Almost/Strong) gives progressive feedback; meters coach, errors punish after the fact.
Minimize time-to-dopamine: Front-load the first value moment (onboarding delight or core value) as fast as possible; attention spans are shorter than ever.
Emulate validated top-app patterns: Borrow onboarding/UX patterns from leading products that already A/B-tested them; don't reinvent the wheel.
Build a coherent brand world: Ads through settings menu share one coherent feel and messaging; be intentional about the world and the customer's role in it.
Cut the fluff (simplicity wins): Delete unused, non-core features; every extra feature distracts from the 80/20 value; world-class products are simple.
Be opinionated: With commoditized software, a clear point of view on how your product should work repels some but creates super-fans.
Smooth gradients only: Use analogous, smooth gradient stops; avoid clashing high-saturation hue pairs that read as noise.
Skip option in onboarding: Onboarding screens must offer Skip alongside Next; never force the tour.
Descriptive input placeholders: Hint what to type (Artists, Albums, Songs...); never a bare Search.
Top-aligned form labels (single axis): Labels above inputs on one left edge; side-by-side labels cause zig-zag scanning.
Split long forms into steps + progress: Wizard with progress indicator and Skip/Next; never one endless scroll.
Avoid pure #000000 / #FFFFFF: Use off-black (~#242424) and off-white (~#E7E9EB) to soften contrast.
Inline, specific errors (where + why): Flag the exact field and failed rule inline; never a generic Error-found banner.
Match input shape to data shape: Segmented one-char-per-box fields for OTP/verification codes, not a single free-text input.
Input masks for formatted data: Auto-formatting masks (MM/DD/YYYY, (+___) __ ___ ___) guide entry for dates/phones.
Correct choice controls: Radio buttons for single-choice, checkboxes for multi-choice; never swapped.
Touch-native pickers on mobile: Scroll-wheel/bottom-sheet pickers for time/date on touch devices, not desktop dropdowns.
Group related elements together: Keep similar/related items contiguous (Gestalt proximity); never interleave unrelated items between them.
Human-like microcopy: Conversational button copy (Looks Good, Take a new photo) over system jargon (Confirm and continue, Retake Photo).
Boxed inputs over underlines: Bordered form fields; underline-only fields have weak affordance.
One dominant primary action: The key CTA gets filled/highlighted treatment; equal-weight CTAs hide the happy path.
Show all options for 2-3 choices: Visible radios/segmented controls, not a dropdown, for tiny choice sets.
Simple readable fonts: Clean UI typefaces (Inter/Poppins/Manrope); decorative display fonts (Italiana/Reggae One/Aclonica) hurt readability.
Error messages do three things: What happened, why it happened, and a clear next action; neither raw stack dumps nor vague Something-went-wrong.
Semantic color system: Consistent info/success/warning/danger scales (lightest-to-darkest) instead of ad-hoc colors; users know the conventions daily.
Strip AI-added clutter: Delete gratuitous descriptive paragraphs, explanatory text, and decorative elements AI adds; if an element isn't useful, remove it.
CTA above the fold: Primary call-to-action visible without scrolling on every key page.
Thank-you/confirmation page after enquiry: Post-submission page confirming receipt and setting next steps.
Response-time promise: State a concrete reply SLA (e.g., we answer within 24h) as trust copy.
Sticky mobile CTA: Persistent bottom-fixed call-to-action on mobile.
Case-studies section: Proof-of-work content showing real outcomes.

Never gate essential actions behind hover: Touch has no hover; the first tap is spent becoming a fake sticky :hover. Hover reveals extras only; primary action always visible, with a touch home (in-card buttons, swipe layer, bottom sheet).
Pointer-based media queries: Branch on @media (hover: hover) / (pointer: coarse), never user-agent sniffing; one query covers laptop+mouse, phone, tablet+mouse.
Pad the hit area, not the icon: Icon stays ~20px; pad the tappable box to 44px+ (HIG 44pt / Material 48dp).
ai_discoverability: LLM context files: Ship an llms.txt for AI agents.
AI crawler permissions: Don't blanket-block AI crawlers in robots.txt.
pre_build_documentation_and_planning: PRD: Define idea overview, core features, and what you're building before coding.
TDD: The bible of tech decisions; stack, tools, APIs, architecture.
Backend schema: Map tables, fields, data types, and relationships upfront.
Engineering plan: Small tasks, strict build order, dependencies, and acceptance criteria.
Steer AI with curated design references: Copy full prompts/style/layout specs or component blocks (Neuform, Superdesign, Efferd) into your agent.
Connect your agent via MCP servers: Secure, permission-enforced access to external tools, databases, and data sources.
Chrome DevTools MCP for live debugging: Let the agent control/inspect a live browser (console, network, performance).
Figma Context MCP for design-to-code: Feed simplified Figma layout/styling data to the agent.

Install a curated agent stack: Plugins (role-specialist toolkits), skills (one-line workflow shortcuts), and MCP servers (Slack/Notion/Zapier/Perplexity/agent-browser, etc.) turn the AI from a chat window into an operations layer.

stack_exclusions.why: Items the 181-item bar contains that Zero-Lag cannot satisfy on Expo + Vercel Hobby at budget zero, with no live host yet. Not failures. Do not open work for them unless the user asks.

items.item: Async job queues for heavy tasks
items.reason: No broker. Vercel Hobby has no long-running workers.
Vercel serverless handles this when a backend exists. Nothing to configure now.
No database has been named yet. Do not invent Redis, Kafka, or a paid DB.
No Postgres. If Firestore is added, authorisation is server-side. If Postgres is added, RLS becomes open work.
Applies only if raw SQL is ever added.
Pre-launch, single maintainer. Revisit at real traffic.
Zero-Lag is not a local business.
No public site yet. JSON-LD applies when public pages exist. LocalBusiness does not.
Rate limiting is the budget-zero control. Add it when a public endpoint exists.
No datastore named yet. Provider-at-rest encryption is enough until the user asks otherwise.
Domain purchase costs money. No live host has been named.
No Figma file and no MCP server.

items.reason: Optional. Nothing in the repo depends on MCP.

mobile_note: Many ui_ux_and_branding items assume a web DOM. On React Native apply the intent, not the literal CSS. They apply literally to any later public HTML.
